Let $Z$ be symmetric positive definite and $p\in\Delta_X$. Then $p$
minimizes $E$ if and only if
\[
 (Zp)_i=E(p)\quad\text{when }p_i>0,
 \qquad (Zp)_j\geq E(p)\quad\text{for all }j.
\]

\[
 p_* = \frac1{1290598}(333299,456400,0,44499,456400)^T,
 \qquad E(p_*)=\frac{9232505841}{10324784000}.

positive mass in the unique optimum.

no_target_yet.statement:
Let $X=\{a_i/1000:0\leq i\leq7\}\subset\mathbb R^4$ with ordinary
Euclidean distance, and $Z_{ij}=\exp(-D_{ij}/1000)$.
Every nonempty principal submatrix of $Z$ is positive definite.
Deletion removes exactly indices $6,7$ at its first step and stops at
the second solve, with probability $p$ supported on $\{0,\ldots,5\}$.
For $p'=(999/1000)p+(1/1000)e_6$,
\[
 \frac{57}{10^9}< E(p)-E(p') <\frac{59}{10^9}.
\]
Thus the Euclidean part of Bouafia's Open problem has answer no.

no_target_yet.statement:
Let $D$ be a finite symmetric distance matrix strictly negative definite
on $\mathbf1^\perp$. Suppose deletion using the stationary solves for
$p^TDp$ has no zero coordinates in any active solve, stops at a positive
probability $u$, and has $(Du)_j>u^TDu$ at a deleted index $j$.
Then deletion for $Z(t)_{ij}=e^{-tD_{ij}}$ is suboptimal for every
sufficiently small $t>0$, with the same sequence of active sets.

no_target_yet.statement:
The five-point scaled-Hamming failure persists on an open interval of
positive scales containing $\log(20/19)$. For every integer $n\geq5$,
some $n$-point negative-type metric has suboptimal deletion output.

distance in $\mathbb R^{n-4}$.
